_metadata.rubric: owner-clarified rubric with calibration anchors + no-literal-false-facts reminder, 2026-10-18
_metadata.independence: I read only u31-blind-input.json; no other repository file, search, web or paid API was used.

hints.reason: SPIDER: a tarantula is a spider; ROCK: no recognizable route beyond "tarantulas hide under rocks", which is invented rescue.
ROCK: a crevice is a crack in rock (rock crevice); SPIDER: the familiar scene of a spider hiding in a crack or crevice.

best_available.why: Only hint that reaches both sides, via the spider-in-a-rock-crack scene.

pairs.pair_note: Thin pair; CREVICE is a moderate scene hint, TARANTULA is spider-only.

hints.reason: SPRING: hot spring is a fixed compound; ROCK: "hot rocks"/hot-stone imagery or geothermally heated rock is a weaker route.
SPRING: spring water; ROCK: only a loose image of water flowing from rock, no fixed phrase.
ROCK: rocks are made of minerals; SPRING: mineral spring / mineral water.

best_available.why: Shared property that reaches both words cleanly: rocks are mineral, springs are mineral springs.

pairs.pair_note: MINERAL is the clear winner; HOT and WATER lean on the spring side.

hints.reason: STAR: shooting star; ROCK: a shooting star is a meteor (true, a space rock burning up) but "shooting" does not point at ROCK for most players.
ROCK: rock music; STAR: a music star; together the familiar compound "rock star".
ROCK: rock guitar; STAR: the rock-star-with-a-guitar scene.

best_available.why: Points straight at the compound "rock star" through rock music and music star.

pairs.pair_note: Good pair; the "rock star" compound carries MUSIC and GUITAR.

hints.reason: ROCK: rock and roll; TRAIN: trains roll (rolling stock), backed by the AC/DC song "Rock 'n' Roll Train".
ROCK: tunnels are bored through rock; TRAIN: the train tunnel scene.
ROCK: mining rock/ore; TRAIN: mine train (mining railway, the familiar mine-train ride).

best_available.why: Concrete shared scene: a train going through a tunnel cut in rock.

pairs.pair_note: Rich pair with three working routes.

hints.reason: WITCH: the witch's cauldron; ROCK: no route.
ROCK: standing stones; WITCH: only via modern pagans/Wiccans gathering at solstice, and most players link Stonehenge to druids, not witches.

best_available.why: Only hint touching both words; the witch side is a pagan-gathering stretch.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Do not explain STONEHENGE as built or used by witches (that would be a wrong fact).

hints.reason: WOLF: wolf den; ROCK: dens in rocky caves or under boulders is a possible but weak scene.
WOLF: wolves howl; ROCK: only the poster image of a wolf howling from a rocky crag, where the rock is incidental.

best_available.why: A rocky den is a real place; HOWL leaves ROCK as scenery.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; both hints are wolf-led.

hints.reason: ROSE: rose water; SALT: salt water; compound route on both sides.
ROSE: desert rose (plant, crystal, Sting song); SALT: salt desert/salt flats is real but a weaker association.
SALT: salt preserves food; ROSE: rose-petal or rose-hip preserves are niche.

best_available.why: Two everyday compounds: rose water and salt water.

pairs.pair_note: WATER is solid; the others lean on one side.

hints.reason: Brand route: Amy Rose and Shadow the Hedgehog are both well-known Sonic characters.
ROSE: roses wilt; SHADOW: no route.
ROSE: a rose fades; SHADOW: shadows fade; a generic verb that reaches neither strongly.
SHADOW: near-synonym (shade); ROSE: "rose" as a shade of pink or roses in the shade, both weak.
ROSE: the black rose symbol; SHADOW: shadows look dark, a visual colour link only.

best_available.why: Only hint that names a real shared context for both words (two Sonic characters).

pairs.pair_note: SONIC depends on gaming familiarity; the rest are generic or one-sided.

hints.reason: ROSE: Rose is the Titanic heroine; SHARK: no sharks in the story, so any shark explanation would be invented.
ROSE: rose thorns; SHARK: no recognizable route.

best_available.why: Strong on ROSE and at least sets an ocean scene; still does not reach SHARK.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; both hints are rose-only. The pair needs a new hint.

hints.reason: ROSE: rose thorns; SNAKE: no route (thorns are not fangs).
SNAKE: snake bite; ROSE: roses do not bite, no route.
ROSE: rose garden; SNAKE: garden snake / the serpent in the Garden of Eden.

best_available.why: Familiar compounds on both sides: rose garden and garden snake.

pairs.pair_note: GARDEN carries the pair; THORN and BITE are one-sided.

hints.reason: ROSE: rose thorns; SPIDER: no route.
ROSE: rose garden; SPIDER: garden spider (a common name) and the garden-web scene.

best_available.why: Rose garden and garden spider are both familiar phrases.

pairs.pair_note: GARDEN works; THORN is filler.

hints.reason: ROSE: compass rose; STAR: navigating by the stars (the North Star as a compass), and the compass rose is drawn as a star.
Story route: The Little Prince loves his rose and lives on a tiny asteroid among the stars.

best_available.why: The Little Prince story holds both the rose and the stars.

pairs.pair_note: Two moderate hints; both depend on recognizing a specific reference.

hints.reason: TRAIN: the train of a wedding dress; ROSE: wedding roses and bouquets.
TRAIN: the bride's train; ROSE: the bride's roses; same scene as WEDDING.

best_available.why: The wedding scene holds both the dress train and the roses.

pairs.pair_note: Clean pair; BRIDE is a variant of WEDDING.

hints.reason: Contains both ROSE and WATER as substrings, which breaks the rule.
ROSE: roses in a vase; WATER: a vase holds water.
ROSE: rose petals; WATER: petals floating on water is a loose image.

best_available.why: The everyday scene of roses standing in a vase of water.

pairs.pair_note: ROSEWATER fails the contains-target rule; VASE is the safe hint.

hints.reason: WITCH: casts spells; ROSE: the spell on the enchanted rose in Beauty and the Beast and on Briar Rose in Sleeping Beauty.
WITCH: an enchantress is a near-synonym; ROSE: the Beauty and the Beast enchantress who leaves the enchanted rose.
ROSE: Briar Rose (Sleeping Beauty's name, and the wild rose); WITCH: only through Maleficent, a wicked fairy that players may or may not call a witch.

best_available.why: Directly evokes the enchanted-rose story and sits close to WITCH.

pairs.pair_note: Fairy-tale pair; ENCHANTRESS is nearly a synonym of WITCH, worth a second opinion.

hints.reason: ROSE: the enchanted rose in Beauty and the Beast; WOLF: a wolf is a beast, and wolves attack Belle in the same film.
ROSE: red roses ("roses are red"); WOLF: Little Red Riding Hood and the wolf (story name route).

best_available.why: Reaches both broadly: red roses and Little Red Riding Hood's wolf.

pairs.pair_note: Both hints work; RED is more immediate.

hints.reason: SALT: season with salt; SHADOW: no route.
SHADOW: "beyond a shadow of a doubt"; SALT: "take it with a grain of salt" means to doubt it; idiom route on both sides.
SALT: salt deserts/flats; SHADOW: "rain shadow" deserts, a geography term few players will reach.

best_available.why: Two familiar idioms of doubt: shadow of a doubt and grain of salt.

pairs.pair_note: DOUBT is clever but indirect on the salt side.

hints.reason: SALT: sea salt; SHARK: sharks live in the sea.
SALT: the salty ocean; SHARK: ocean predator; same route as SEA.

best_available.why: Sea salt is a fixed phrase and the sea is the shark's home.

pairs.pair_note: Easy pair; OCEAN duplicates SEA.

hints.reason: SNAKE: desert snakes (rattlesnakes); SALT: salt deserts/flats are real but a weaker association.
SALT: sea salt; SNAKE: sea snake, a real animal.
SALT: salt lick; SNAKE: snakes flick their tongues rather than lick, so no fair route.

best_available.why: Two compounds: sea salt and sea snake.

pairs.pair_note: SEA works; LICK would need a false "snakes lick" claim.

hints.reason: SALT: sprinkle salt; SPIDER: no route.
SALT: salt crystals; SPIDER: no recognizable route.

best_available.why: Strong on SALT; nothing reaches SPIDER, so it is a default only.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; both hints are salt-only. The pair needs a new hint.

hints.reason: SPRING: the spring thaw; SALT: road salt thaws ice; shared verb route.
SALT: salt water; SPRING: spring water; compound route on both sides.
SALT: salt is a mineral (mineral salts); SPRING: mineral spring.

best_available.why: Two everyday compounds: salt water and spring water.

pairs.pair_note: Three working hints.

hints.reason: SALT: salted crackers/saltines; STAR: no route.
SALT: salted pretzels; STAR: no route.

best_available.why: Default only; both hints are salt snack foods with nothing for STAR.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; both hints are one-sided. Something like SEA (sea salt / sea star) would reach both.

hints.reason: SALT: Salt Lake (City); TRAIN: only via the transcontinental railroad's golden spike in Utah, a history stretch.
TRAIN: freight train; SALT: salt is hauled as bulk freight, but there is no familiar link.

best_available.why: Strongest single side (Salt Lake) with a real, if niche, railroad history link.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; both hints reach only one side clearly.

hints.reason: Brine is salt water: both words in one definition, the familiar pickling brine.
Compound route: saltwater taffy.
The ocean is salt water.
The sea is salt water; same route as OCEAN.

best_available.why: Brine simply is salt water.

pairs.pair_note: Very easy pair; four passing hints.

hints.reason: WITCH: protective wards and magic; SALT: the folklore of salt warding off evil.
SALT: the protective salt circle trope; WITCH: the witch's magic circle / coven circle.
WITCH: the Salem witch trials; SALT: no route (the name only looks like SALT).

best_available.why: The salt circle and the witch's circle are both familiar occult images.

pairs.pair_note: Folklore pair; SALEM is witch-only.

hints.reason: WOLF: wolf hunter; SALT: no recognizable route.
SALT: salt lick; WOLF: wolves lick (pups, wounds, "licking its wounds"), a weak generic animal link.

best_available.why: Strong salt compound with a weak but true wolf link.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; the pair needs a new hint.

hints.reason: SHARK: Jaws; SHADOW: only a vague image of a dark shape under water.
SHARK: shark fin; SHADOW: no route.

best_available.why: Strong shark side; the lurking dark-shape image is the only thing near SHADOW.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; both hints are shark-only.

hints.reason: SNAKE: snake in the grass; SHADOW: no route.
SHADOW: lurking in the shadows; SNAKE: a lurking snake, the ambush predator.
SNAKE: a snake strikes; SHADOW: "strike from the shadows" is a weaker phrase.

best_available.why: Lurking in the shadows is a fixed image, and snakes are the classic lurker.

pairs.pair_note: LURK carries the pair; STRIKE is close behind.

hints.reason: SHADOW: lurking in the shadows; SPIDER: a spider lurking in its web.
SPIDER: spiders and cobwebs in corners; SHADOW: dark, shadowy corners.

best_available.why: A clear shared verb: things lurk in shadows and spiders lurk in webs.

pairs.pair_note: Both hints are moderate, and they work together.

hints.reason: SHADOW: the sun casts shadows; SPRING: spring sunshine is only a loose link.
SHADOW: shadow length; SPRING: no clear route (seasonal day length is a rescue).
Story route: on Groundhog Day, whether the groundhog sees his shadow decides whether spring comes early.

best_available.why: The Groundhog Day story ties shadow to an early spring.

pairs.pair_note: GROUNDHOG is excellent; LENGTH should go.

hints.reason: SHADOW: an eclipse is a shadow; STAR: only because the sun is a star, a step most players will not take.
STAR: starlight; SHADOW: light and shadow, a familiar contrast.

best_available.why: Starlight plus the light-and-shadow pairing reaches both words.

pairs.pair_note: LIGHT works; ECLIPSE is borderline.

hints.reason: TRAIN: ghost train (fairground ride, phantom trains); SHADOW: shadows as ghostly shapes is only a mood link.
TRAIN: train tunnel; SHADOW: tunnels are dark and shadowy, a mood link only.

best_available.why: Ghost train is a real compound, and ghosts and shadows share a spooky sense.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; SHADOW is reached only by mood in both hints.

hints.reason: WATER: deep water; SHADOW: deep shadows; a shared adjective in common phrases.
WATER: a reflection in water; SHADOW: your shadow and your reflection are both your image cast by light.
SHADOW: near-synonym; WATER: only the "shade and water" phrase from heat-safety advice.

best_available.why: A water reflection and a shadow are the two familiar "copies" of you made by light.

pairs.pair_note: Moderate pair; SHADE is close to a synonym of SHADOW.

hints.reason: WITCH: the classic Halloween witch; SHADOW: spooky shadows are only a mood link.
WITCH: the witch's broomstick; SHADOW: a broom silhouette against the moon is not a shadow.
SHADOW: shadows are dark; WITCH: dark magic and the dark witch; shared property.

best_available.why: Shared property: shadows are dark and witches practise dark magic.

pairs.pair_note: Weak-moderate pair; DARK is the only PASS and it is generic.

hints.reason: SHADOW: shadow puppets; WOLF: the classic wolf hand-shadow.
WOLF: wolves howl; SHADOW: no route.

best_available.why: The wolf is one of the best-known hand-shadow puppets.

pairs.pair_note: PUPPET carries the pair.

hints.reason: SHARK: shark bite; SNAKE: snake bite; both fixed compounds.
Shared property: both are famous predators.
Shared property: both are classic feared animals (Jaws, fear of snakes).

best_available.why: Shark bite and snake bite are both everyday phrases.

pairs.pair_note: Easy pair with three valid routes.

hints.reason: Shared property: both are predators.
Shared property: both are classic phobias (arachnophobia, fear of sharks).

best_available.why: Spiders and sharks are the two most commonly feared animals.

pairs.pair_note: Both hints are generic but valid shared properties.

hints.reason: SPRING: to spring is to leap (near-synonym of the verb); SHARK: sharks breaching or "jump the shark", which uses JUMP, not LEAP.
SPRING: spring break; SHARK: no route.

best_available.why: Reaches SPRING as a verb and SHARK through breaching or the "jump the shark" idiom.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. JUMP (jump the shark / jump as spring) would be stronger.

hints.reason: STAR: sea star (starfish); SHARK: sharks live in the sea.
SHARK: Jaws; STAR: only "film star", which does not tie to the shark.

best_available.why: Sea star is a real name for the starfish, and the sea is the shark's home.

pairs.pair_note: SEA works; JAWS is shark-only.

hints.reason: TRAIN: bullet train; SHARK: no route (there is no common "bullet shark"; the bull shark does not count).
SHARK: shark tank (aquarium and TV show); TRAIN: tank engine (Thomas the Tank Engine) and tank cars.

best_available.why: Shark Tank and Thomas the Tank Engine are both familiar.

pairs.pair_note: TANK is a nice double compound; BULLET is train-only.
